acceptance.completion: Every applicable case has evidence and an independent PASS tied to the delivered implementation. Unspecified, untested, and unreviewed cases remain incomplete. The entire gallery CPU frame must additionally satisfy the performance gate for every component acceptance.
acceptance.themes: light and dark, every built-in palette, and reference baseline
acceptance.review_invalidation: Any implementation change invalidates affected prior PASS verdicts until independently reviewed again.

performance.status: failed: measured native startup scopes exceed 2ms; other scenarios and WASM timing remain unverified
performance.scope: entire gallery frame, on both desktop and wasm-browser; applies to acceptance of every component
performance.metric: CPU frame elapsed time including view rendering, layout, prepaint, paint, scene finalization and graphics command submission
performance.submission_timing: Keep synchronous drawable acquisition and submission elapsed time in the complete frame budget, including cleanup. API-call elapsed time may be reported separately for diagnosis, but must not be subtracted to establish the <= 2 ms gate; it is not a measurement of pure blocking or GPU time.
performance.comparison: less than or equal to; any measured frame > 2.0 ms fails
performance.aggregation: maximum per-frame duration; also report median, p95, p99 and over-budget count
performance.first_frame: included; report cold-start and steady-state separately without excluding slow frames from acceptance
performance.gpu: measure and report separately; never substitute GPU or average FPS for CPU frame time
evidence_required: exact source commit and dirty-worktree status
release build profile and build flags
hardware, OS, browser and graphics backend
viewport, device pixel ratio, zoom, theme and text scale
per-frame raw timings and timing boundaries
frame count, maximum and over-budget count
performance.completion: No component or gallery can pass without whole-gallery evidence at or below the budget. Existing functional or visual reviews do not establish performance acceptance.

scrolling_fps.status: failed: native release local wheel-input scrolling measured a minimum full-window 58.5115 FPS; complete Gallery traversal and strict per-submission timing remain unverified
scrolling_fps.diagnostic_review: independent subagent verified dispatch-based wheel input, actual movement, Disabled backend VSync readback, stable source and binary identities, 598 of 601 CPU scopes over 2ms, enabled Fast retention with observed reuse, and incomplete Gallery coverage. A prior source-drift run is retained separately and not accepted; this is a reviewed failure, not conformance PASS
scrolling_fps.scenario: continuous upward and downward scrolling through the complete Gallery, including newly exposed component rows and direction reversals
scrolling_fps.metric: actual rendered frame submissions during the declared active scrolling interval; not frame requests, monitor refresh rate, or skipped/no-drawable submission attempts
scrolling_fps.synchronization: measure with vertical synchronization disabled where the backend exposes this capability; report actual synchronization state and request pacing; unsupported browser/platform control is not a PASS
evidence_required: frame intervals and minimum FPS, with the sampling definition stated
all slow intervals during the declared continuous scrolling scenario
CPU scope timings, GPU measurements separately
scrolling_fps.cpu_budget: the existing <= 2ms whole-gallery CPU frame gate remains required independently
scrolling_fps.interpretation: rendering/submission throughput; physical monitor refresh is reported separately

objective: Reproduce every component of Google's Figma Material 3 Design Kit plus the union of https://md3.io/ and https://m3e.kyralabs.dev/ components, styles and animations on desktop and WASM galleries, with priority Figma kit > md3.io > m3e.kyralabs.dev per value; use https://gpui-kit.com/ for gallery organization. Exact visual and animation parity, independent subagent approval for every component, whole-gallery CPU frames <= 2 ms and continuous vertical-scrolling rendering throughput >= 500 FPS, atomic commits and frequent GitHub progress pushes are required. Material icons must come from the gpui-material-symbols repository, pinned by Git revision for default builds; its sibling checkout may be used explicitly for development and improved as needed. Build on Longbridge gpui-kit and its gpui-component layer, reusing existing controls and infrastructure before implementing Material-specific differences.

reference_policy.priority_rule: Per token family (color, shape, type, motion, state, geometry) and per value: use the first reference in priority that defines the value and record that source with the value (rustdoc and fixture). Lower-priority fixtures that are outranked stay as untested secondary evidence.

figma.name: Google Material 3 Design Kit (Figma Community)
figma.extraction: Figma Plugin API in the user's open copy (~/Developer/.figma-tools): local variables, text styles, effect styles and component nodes; values recorded with node/style/variable ids in each figma-*.json fixture
figma.defines: baseline color scheme (6 modes), type scale and emphasized styles, font theme, shape scale, elevation effect styles, state-layer opacities, component geometry and colors. It defines no motion values.

reference_policy.scope: union of all components and their variants from both sites
reference_policy.overlap: Superseded: overlaps are resolved per value by `priority`, not per component.
reference_policy.existing_reference_field: Top-level `reference` pins md3.io (floor/material) provenance; it is authoritative only where token_sources names md3.io.
reference_policy.existing_evidence: Fixtures from an outranked source remain secondary evidence and are not tested; they do not establish conformance.
reference_policy.catalog_status: top-level union enumerated; variant and alias coverage still requires source and rendered-site audit

token_sources.note: Which reference each crate token family comes from under `priority`. Figma values are extracted with the Figma Plugin API; m3e values by scripts/extract-m3e-tokens.py; md3.io values by the capture scripts. A matching fixture is token evidence, not a conformance PASS.
